rationale: B wins because it is stricter about what the update can actually support. A's "Oatly is still losing money. Its new formula for profitability involves fewer factories and a bigger café footprint" is a tempting business story, but it starts writing management's strategy for them. B's "Oatly wins its biggest pour-volume deal in the same quarter it closes a US plant" has its own invented phrase problem, but the set does a better job calling out missing proof instead of decorating around it.
gaps_in_A: "customers who don't specify get oat milk" overreads "default non-dairy option." The update does not say oat milk becomes the default milk for all customers, or even define how the chain uses "default."
"falling volumes, shrinking retail shelf space, canceled expansions" is unsupported background color. Maybe true in the market, but it is not in the supplied update.

"Oatly bets rightsizing beats scaling" and "new formula for profitability" impose a strategy the facts do not prove. The update says cost cuts, a plant closure, a partnership, and a narrowing loss. That is not yet a thesis.

The third and fourth kept angles both run on the same engine: plant closure plus unprofitability plus cafe footprint. The investor version needs harder financial proof or it becomes a padded sibling of the contrarian angle.
gaps_in_B: "biggest pour-volume deal" is invented. The update gives 1,400 locations, not biggest, not pour volume, and not deal size.
"same quarter" is too precise for the supplied facts. The update gives current rollout context and last-quarter loss context; it does not establish that every move lands in the same quarter.

The first headline, "cuts climate footprint 31% per liter, verified by third-party LCA," mostly repeats the announcement. The body correctly finds the better story: what the LCA proves, who paid for it, and what the boundary was.
"landing more demand while cutting US manufacturing footprint" is plausible but not proven. The set should say the deal may increase demand, then require volume and sourcing proof.
